elements.name: Composed Method
elements.what: Structure a method as a short sequence of calls to other intention-named methods, all at a single level of abstraction.
elements.problem: Long methods that mix abstraction levels are hard to read, reuse, and override; dividing behavior into small, identically-leveled named steps yields composable, self-documenting units.
elements.named_in: Beck, Smalltalk Best Practice Patterns (Prentice Hall, 1997), 'Composed Method'
elements.borderline: sits near practice territory (method-writing guidance), kept: a named pattern in a canonical pattern catalog describing a concrete code construct

elements.name: Method Object
aka: Replace Method with Method Object (Fowler, Refactoring)
elements.what: Reify a complex method as its own class: parameters and local variables become instance variables, the body becomes small methods on the new object.
elements.problem: A method whose many temporaries and parameters resist decomposition can be split freely once its working state lives in a dedicated object.
elements.named_in: Beck, Smalltalk Best Practice Patterns (1997), 'Method Object'; Fowler, Refactoring (1999) names the move 'Replace Method with Method Object'

elements.name: Exceptional Value
elements.what: A distinguished value object representing missing or invalid input that flows through the domain model, absorbing or rejecting messages instead of raising errors.
elements.problem: Real-world input contains blanks and illegible entries; letting a typed placeholder value propagate keeps exceptional-case handling concentrated near the UI instead of scattered through business logic, while still recording that the input was bad.
elements.named_in: Cunningham, The CHECKS Pattern Language of Information Integrity (PLoP 1994; c2.com/ppr/checks.html)
elements.borderline: adjacent to null-object and special-case (both indexed); kept as the CHECKS-named propagate-through-computation mechanism the mission explicitly seeds

elements.name: Units-of-Measure Types
aka: dimensional analysis in the type system
elements.what: Encode physical units and dimensions as type-level annotations so the compiler checks unit correctness and infers result units through arithmetic, with no runtime cost.
elements.problem: Mixing quantities of different units (feet vs meters, ms vs s) compiles silently with raw numerics; type-level units turn unit mistakes into type errors.
elements.named_in: Kennedy, Types for Units-of-Measure: Theory and Practice (CEFP 2009, LNCS 6299); Kennedy, Programming Languages and Dimensions (Cambridge TR 391, 1996); shipped in F# 2.0

elements.name: Disruptor
elements.what: A pre-allocated ring buffer where producers and consumers coordinate through monotonic sequence counters and sequence barriers instead of locks, supporting dependency graphs of consumers over the same entries.
elements.problem: Bounded queues concentrate contention on head and tail and add latency per pipeline stage; sequence-gated access to a shared ring gives orders-of-magnitude lower latency and lets multiple consumers process entries in dependency order without copying.
elements.named_in: Thompson, Farley, Barker, Gee, Stewart — Disruptor: High Performance Alternative to Bounded Queues for Exchanging Data Between Concurrent Threads (LMAX technical paper, 2011)

elements.name: Operational Transformation
elements.what: Keep concurrently edited replicas consistent by transforming each incoming operation against the concurrent operations already applied locally, preserving intention and causality without locking.
elements.problem: Optimistic concurrent editing of shared data (collaborative text editors) requires every replica to converge to the same state while staying responsive; transforming operations reorders their effects instead of blocking users.
elements.named_in: Ellis & Gibbs, Concurrency Control in Groupware Systems (ACM SIGMOD 1989, pp. 399-407)

elements.name: Functional Options
elements.what: A constructor takes a variadic list of option functions, each of which mutates the value being configured; options are first-class values that can be composed, defaulted, and added without breaking callers.
elements.problem: Constructors with many optional parameters degenerate into config structs or telescoping overloads; closures-as-options keep the zero-option case clean and the API forward-compatible.
elements.named_in: Pike, Self-referential functions and the design of options (commandcenter blog, 2014); Cheney, Functional options for friendly APIs (dave.cheney.net / dotGo, 2014)

elements.name: Structured Concurrency
elements.what: Concurrent tasks may only be spawned inside a lexical scope (nursery / task scope) that cannot be exited until all child tasks complete, so errors and cancellation propagate through a tree of scopes.
elements.problem: Fire-and-forget spawning (go statement, detached threads) breaks local reasoning, error propagation, and cancellation; binding task lifetimes to block structure restores them, analogous to structured programming's elimination of goto.
elements.named_in: Smith, Notes on structured concurrency, or: Go statement considered harmful (vorpus.org, 2018); Trio nursery documentation; JEP 453: Structured Concurrency (JDK 21)

elements.name: Feature Flag
elements.what: Toggle points in code consult a toggle router that decides from configuration or request context which of two codepaths runs, changing system behavior without changing code.
elements.problem: Shipping incomplete work on trunk, dark launches, A/B experiments, kill switches, and per-user permissions all need latent codepaths selectable at runtime or deploy time rather than at merge time.
elements.named_in: Hodgson, Feature Toggles (aka Feature Flags), martinfowler.com (2017); Fowler, FeatureToggle bliki (2010)
elements.borderline: the delivery-process side (trunk-based development, flag hygiene) is practice territory and excluded; kept for the in-program toggle-point / toggle-router mechanism Hodgson catalogs

elements.name: Template Engine
aka: Template View (P of EAA web specialization)
elements.what: Produce output text by interpolating data-model values and evaluating restricted directives (conditionals, loops, includes) inside a template document that fixes the static structure of the output.
elements.problem: Generating HTML, code, or reports by string concatenation entangles logic with presentation; a template engine separates the output's static shape from the data that fills it, ideally enforcing strict model-view separation.
elements.named_in: Parr, Enforcing Strict Model-View Separation in Template Engines (WWW 2004, StringTemplate); Fowler, Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (2002) names the web form 'Template View'

elements.name: Dictionary Encoding
elements.what: Replace repeated wide values in a column with small fixed-width integer codes indexing a dictionary of the distinct values; operators can often work directly on the codes.
elements.problem: Low-cardinality columns waste space and memory bandwidth storing the same strings repeatedly; integer codes compress the data and make scans and comparisons cheaper, especially in columnar layouts.
elements.named_in: Abadi, Boncz, Harizopoulos, Idreos, Madden — The Design and Implementation of Modern Column-Oriented Database Systems (Foundations and Trends in Databases 5(3), 2013)

excluded_notable.name: Semantic Data Types (mission anchor phrase)
excluded_notable.why: No published source names this exact phrase as a design element (searched, including White's Making Embedded Systems). The mechanism is covered by newtype + value-object + quantity + Whole Value (already an aka of newtype, verified live in Cunningham's CHECKS at c2.com/ppr/checks.html), now extended by the new units-of-measure-types entry. Anchor considered covered.

excluded_notable.name: Asynchronous Programming Models (mission anchor phrase)
excluded_notable.why: Umbrella term, not one mechanism. Covered in the index by async-await-model, coroutine, future-promise, event-loop, proactor, green-threads, protothread, continuation-passing-style. Anchor considered covered; nothing added.

excluded_notable.name: Binding Properties (charter seed, attributed to Grand 1998)
excluded_notable.why: Attribution did not verify live: Wikipedia's 'Binding properties pattern' credits Victor Porton, not Grand, and searches of Grand's Patterns in Java vol 1 contents did not surface it. The mechanism (synchronize properties across objects via change observers) is the indexed data-binding element (aka already includes 'property binding'). Recommend adding 'Binding Properties' and 'bound properties (JavaBeans API spec 1.01, 1997)' to data-binding's aka rather than creating a duplicate.

excluded_notable.name: Whole Value (Cunningham CHECKS)
excluded_notable.why: Verified live (c2.com/ppr/checks.html) but already folded into the index as an aka of newtype; kept folded per the dedup rule. Integrator may prefer promoting it to a standalone element since it is the closest published name for the 'semantic data types' anchor; if promoted, remove it from newtype's aka.

notes: Charter resolution. (1) 'semantic data types' anchor: the exact phrase is not an established element name in any source found (checked White's Making Embedded Systems via search; only unrelated semantic-web literature uses the phrase). Coverage story: newtype, value-object, quantity, smart-data already indexed; Whole Value (Cunningham, CHECKS, PLoP 1994 - live-verified) is folded as newtype aka; added units-of-measure-types (Kennedy) as the missing type-level member of the family. (2) 'asynchronous programming models' anchor: already covered by async-await-model (index line 16) plus coroutine/future-promise/event-loop/proactor et al; nothing added. (3) Seeds: 10 of 11 verified and added (Composed Method, Method Object, Exceptional Value, Disruptor, Operational Transformation, Functional Options, Structured Concurrency, Feature Flag, Template Engine, Dictionary Encoding); Binding Properties deliberately rejected as a duplicate of data-binding with an unverifiable Grand attribution (see excluded_notable). All naming sources confirmed by live search/fetch this session; CHECKS page loaded in full. named_in_corpus_id used only for fowlerref (Fowler, Refactoring) on method-object; Beck SBPP, CHECKS, LMAX paper, Ellis&Gibbs 1989, Kennedy, Parr WWW2004, Abadi et al 2013, Hodgson 2017, Smith 2018 are NOT in work_ids.tsv - flag for Phase 2 as new nodes. INDEX ERRORS SPOTTED: (a) 'adapter' lists 'Decorator' as an aka, and GoF Decorator appears nowhere else in the index - Decorator is a distinct GoF pattern and is effectively MISSING; recommend splitting it out. (b) 'factory-method' lists 'Prototype, clone' as aka, and GoF Prototype appears nowhere else - also a distinct GoF pattern, effectively MISSING; recommend splitting. Those two were not added here (outside charter, and technically present 'under an alias'), but they are the two highest-priority fixes this hunt surfaced. Minor: 'special-case' and the new exceptional-value should get a cross-reference note at integration; 'data-binding' aka should absorb 'Binding Properties' and 'bound properties (JavaBeans)'.
